answer: Each identity's usable standing is released only after a sequential, non-transferable custody period, and the release rate is super-linear in how many identities an operator runs, so a fleet cannot mature faster than one identity at a time. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. The lantern is the serial tenure, the pulse the custody window that must elapse, and the walnut the standing released at the end of it; the lantern is personal, the pulse is not skippable, and the walnut cannot be inherited by a sibling.
